lines.text: Meta built a debugger that can follow a bug from normal code into a graphics chip.
A CPU and a GPU speak different instruction languages and even use different memory maps.
lines.title: Two different worlds

lines.text: Old GPU debuggers were built separately by each chip maker, so shared features were rebuilt again and again.
lines.title: The old way

lines.text: Meta added a plugin layer to lldb-server. The CPU and GPU become two separate targets.
lines.title: The new design

lines.text: The developer still sees one session, and can switch between the CPU and GPU targets.
lines.title: One session

lines.text: Each chip maker only writes its own plugin. Most shared pieces are already in the open-source LLVM project.
lines.title: Takeaways
